record.paper_title: Regularity Properties of Sectorial Operators: Counterexamples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Find an analogue, in the borderline case omega_H-infinity(A) = pi/2, of the characterizations known below the critical angle. On Hilbert spaces, if -A generates a contractive analytic C_0-semigroup then A has a bounded H-infinity calculus with omega_H-infinity(A) = omega(A) < pi/2, and conversely operators with bounded H-infinity calculus of angle less than pi/2 are similar to generators of contractive analytic semigroups. On L^p-spaces, if -A generates a contractive positive analytic C_0-semigroup then A has a bounded H-infinity calculus with angle less than pi/2, and conversely such operators admit the structural model described in Theorem 2.11. What is the correct corresponding characterization when the H-infinity angle is exactly pi/2?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Find a similar characterization as in Theorem 2.10 or Theorem 2.11 in the case ωH∞(A) = π/2.
Theorem 2.10. Let A be a sectorial operator on a Hilbert space such that −A generates a contractive analytic C0-semigroup. Then A has a bounded H∞-calculus with ωH∞(A) = ω(A) < π/2.

Theorem 2.11. Let p ∈ (1, ∞) and A be a sectorial operator on an Lp-space Lp(Ω) such that −A generates a contractive positive analytic C0-semigroup. Then A has a bounded H∞-calculus with ωH∞(A) = ωR(A) < π/2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A closed densely defined linear operator $A$ on a Banach space $X$ is called sectorial of angle $\omega\in[0,\pi)$ if its spectrum is contained in the closed sector $\overline{\Sigma_\omega}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}:|\arg z|\le\omega\}\cup\{0\}$ and for every $\theta\in(\omega,\pi)$ one has $\sup\{\|\lambda(\lambda-A)^{-1}\|:\lambda\notin\overline{\Sigma_\theta}\}<\infty$. The sectoriality angle $\omega(A)$ is the infimum of such $\omega$. For $\theta\in(0,\pi)$, let $H^\infty(\Sigma_\theta)$ denote the algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on $\Sigma_\theta$. One says that $A$ has a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus of angle $\theta$ if the natural functional calculus $f\mapsto f(A)$ extends to a bounded algebra homomorphism $H^\infty(\Sigma_\theta)\to\mathcal{B}(X)$; the $H^\infty$-angle $\omega_{H^\infty}(A)$ is the infimum of such $\theta$. The operator $-A$ generates a contractive analytic $C_0$-semigroup if there exists $\delta\in(0,\pi/2]$ such that $z\mapsto e^{-zA}$ is a holomorphic semigroup on $\Sigma_\delta$ with $\|e^{-zA}\|\le 1$ for all $z\in\Sigma_\delta$.

Known characterizations below the critical angle:
(i) On a Hilbert space $H$, if $-A$ generates a contractive analytic $C_0$-semigroup, then $A$ has a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus with $\omega_{H^\infty}(A)=\omega(A)<\pi/2$; conversely, every sectorial operator on a Hilbert space with bounded $H^\infty$-calculus of angle strictly less than $\pi/2$ is similar to (the negative generator of) a contractive analytic $C_0$-semigroup.
(ii) On $L^p(\Omega)$ with $p\in(1,\infty)$, if $-A$ generates a contractive positive analytic $C_0$-semigroup, then $A$ has a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus with $\omega_{H^\infty}(A)=\omega_R(A)<\pi/2$ (where $\omega_R(A)$ denotes the $R$-sectoriality angle), and a converse structural model is available.

Problem. Provide an analogous characterization in the borderline case $\omega_{H^\infty}(A)=\pi/2$. Specifically, identify a class of sectorial operators on Hilbert spaces (respectively on $L^p$-spaces, $1<p<\infty$) that, up to similarity (resp. up to an analogous structural model), coincides exactly with the class of sectorial operators having a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus of angle exactly $\pi/2$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located surveys and works on $H^\infty$-calculus for sectorial operators (Haase, Le Merdy, and others) which discuss characterizations strictly below the critical angle $\pi/2$, but no source providing the analogous characterization in the borderline case $\omega_{H^\infty}(A)=\pi/2$ was found. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Functional Calculi for Sectorial Operators and Related Function Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Recent survey of holomorphic functional calculi for sectorial operators; treats sub-critical angles but does not provide a characterization at angle π/2.
status_evidence.claim: No characterization at the critical angle π/2 is given in this recent survey.

status_evidence.title: H∞-functional calculus and models of Nagy–Foiaş type for sectorial operators
status_evidence.snippet: A sectorial operator admits an H∞-functional calculus iff it has a Nagy–Foiaş-type functional model; results stated for angles less than π/2.
status_evidence.claim: Structural-model characterizations are available below the critical angle, not at it.

status_evidence.title: The Functional Calculus for Sectorial Operators (Haase)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference on functional calculus for sectorial operators.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference; the borderline case ω_{H∞}(A)=π/2 characterization is not established.
